From a5c0359f5cbc51a2e2b114d6041e0f3c73f903e9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 16:46:13 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] ip6_vti: fix incorrect tunnel matching in vti6_tnl_lookup()

In vti6_tnl_lookup(), when an exact match for a tunnel fails,
the code falls back to searching for wildcard tunnels:

- Tunnels matching the packet's local address, with any remote address
  wildcard remote).

- Tunnels matching the packet's remote address, with any local address
  (wildcard local).

However, vti6 stores all these different types of tunnels in the same
hash table (ip6n->tnls_r_l) prone to hash collisions.

The bug is that the fallback search loops in vti6_tnl_lookup() were
missing checks to ensure that the candidate tunnel actually has
a wildcard address.

Fixes: fbe68ee87522 ("vti6: Add a lookup method for tunnels with wildcard endpoints.")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Reviewed-by: Nicolas Dichtel <nicolas.dichtel@6wind.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260608164613.933023-1-edumazet@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c b/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c
index d2b74a6f2cf6..d871cab6938d 100644
--- a/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c
+++ b/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c
@@ -106,6 +106,7 @@ vti6_tnl_lookup(struct net *net, const struct in6_addr *remote,
 	hash = HASH(&any, local);
 	for_each_vti6_tunnel_rcu(ip6n->tnls_r_l[hash]) {
 		if (ipv6_addr_equal(local, &t->parms.laddr) &&
+		    ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr) &&
 		    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
 			return t;
 	}
@@ -113,6 +114,7 @@ vti6_tnl_lookup(struct net *net, const struct in6_addr *remote,
 	hash = HASH(remote, &any);
 	for_each_vti6_tunnel_rcu(ip6n->tnls_r_l[hash]) {
 		if (ipv6_addr_equal(remote, &t->parms.raddr) &&
+		    ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr) &&
 		    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
 			return t;
 	}

2.34.1

## Patch Summary: Bug Fix in `vti6_tnl_lookup()`

### Modifications in `net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c`

Two lines were added in the `vti6_tnl_lookup()` function, both within fallback search loops that iterate over the hash table of tunnels (`ip6n->tnls_r_l`):

1. **Additional wildcard check for remote address**  
   Line added after the existing condition `ipv6_addr_equal(local, &t->parms.laddr)`:  
   `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr)`  
   This ensures that when looking for a tunnel that matches the packet's local address, the candidate tunnel must also have a wildcard remote address (`raddr` set to `any`).

2. **Additional wildcard check for local address**  
   Line added after the existing condition `ipv6_addr_equal(remote, &t->parms.raddr)`:  
   `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)`  
   This ensures that when looking for a tunnel that matches the packet's remote address, the candidate tunnel must also have a wildcard local address (`laddr` set to `any`).

### Relationship Between Modifications

Both modifications address the same root cause: the original fallback logic was missing checks for address wildcarding, causing the function to potentially match non-wildcard tunnels (with specific remote or local addresses) that happened to collide in the same hash table bucket. This could lead to incorrect tunnel selection. The two additions are symmetric—they enforce that the tunnel is indeed a wildcard endpoint tunnel in each respective lookup direction. They are independent but both required to fully fix the bug.

Here is the commit message:
ip6_vti: fix incorrect tunnel matching in vti6_tnl_lookup()

In vti6_tnl_lookup(), when an exact match for a tunnel fails,
the code falls back to searching for wildcard tunnels:

- Tunnels matching the packet's local address, with any remote address
  wildcard remote).

- Tunnels matching the packet's remote address, with any local address
  (wildcard local).

However, vti6 stores all these different types of tunnels in the same
hash table (ip6n->tnls_r_l) prone to hash collisions.

The bug is that the fallback search loops in vti6_tnl_lookup() were
missing checks to ensure that the candidate tunnel actually has
a wildcard address.

Fixes: fbe68ee87522 ("vti6: Add a lookup method for tunnels with wildcard endpoints.")
Signed-off-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Cc: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Reviewed-by: Nicolas Dichtel <nicolas.dichtel@6wind.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260608164613.933023-1-edumazet@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The fallback search loops in `vti6_tnl_lookup()` for wildcard tunnels did not verify that the candidate tunnel actually had the expected wildcard address (remote or local), causing potential incorrect matching when hash collisions occur with non-wildcard tunnels stored in the same hash table bucket.

Here is the patch:
  **/
 static struct ip6_tnl *
 vti6_tnl_lookup(struct net *net, const struct in6_addr *remote,
 		const struct in6_addr *local)
 {
 	unsigned int hash = HASH(remote, local);
 	struct ip6_tnl *t;
 	struct vti6_net *ip6n = net_generic(net, vti6_net_id);
 	struct in6_addr any;
 
 	for_each_vti6_tunnel_rcu(ip6n->tnls_r_l[hash]) {
 		if (ipv6_addr_equal(local, &t->parms.laddr) &&
 		    ipv6_addr_equal(remote, &t->parms.raddr) &&
 		    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
 			return t;
 	}
 
 	memset(&any, 0, sizeof(any));
 	hash = HASH(&any, local);
 	for_each_vti6_tunnel_rcu(ip6n->tnls_r_l[hash]) {
 		if (ipv6_addr_equal(local, &t->parms.laddr) &&
+		    ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr) &&
 		    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
 			return t;
 	}
 
 	hash = HASH(remote, &any);
 	for_each_vti6_tunnel_rcu(ip6n->tnls_r_l[hash]) {
 		if (ipv6_addr_equal(remote, &t->parms.raddr) &&
+		    ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr) &&
 		    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
 			return t;
 	}
 
 	t = rcu_dereference(ip6n->tnls_wc[0]);
 	if (t && (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
 		return t;
 
 	return NULL;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (ipv6_addr_equal(local, &t->parms.laddr) &&
    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
```
```c

    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
```
Reason:
These two fallback loops aimed to match tunnels with a wildcard endpoint (any address). However, they omitted a check for the presence of that wildcard (`ipv6_addr_any`). Because all tunnel types share the same hash table, a hash collision could cause a non-wildcard tunnel (with both addresses defined) to be incorrectly matched, leading to wrong tunnel selection.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (ipv6_addr_equal(local, &t->parms.laddr) &&
    ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr) &&
    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
```
```c
if (ipv6_addr_equal(remote, &t->parms.raddr) &&
    ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr) &&
    (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP))
```
Reason:
By adding `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr)` and `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)`, the code now explicitly verifies that the candidate tunnel actually has the expected wildcard endpoint. This prevents accidental matching of tunnels that have both addresses specified, ensuring correct fallback behavior.
